title: Toward Dual-Functional LAWN: Control-Aware System Design for Aerodynamics-Aided UAV Formations
venue: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications
originalSiteTitle: Towards Dual-Functional LAWN: Control-Aware System Design for Aerodynamics-Aided UAV Formations
summary: This work connects aerodynamic energy savings with the wireless control of UAV formations. A ground station uses a shared ISAC transmission to guide multiple formations and monitor a target region. A distributed diffusion-LMS procedure lets neighboring UAVs cooperate to form an energy-saving configuration. The beamformer is then designed around the worst control cost, subject to transmit-power and sensing requirements. A combination of successive convex approximation and semidefinite relaxation handles the coupled optimization. Simulations examine how formation geometry and radio-resource design jointly affect energy consumption and control performance.

image.title: Toward Dual-Functional LAWN: Control-Aware System Design for Aerodynamics-Aided UAV Formations
image.caption: Fig. 1: The considered LAWN includes an ISAC-GBS to continuously monitor the formations and sense the pre-determined target area, providing precise guidance to UAV formations flight.

title: LAWNs Meet SWIPT: Beamforming and Power Splitting Optimization for Predictive Control
venue: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications
originalSiteTitle: LAWNs Meet SWIPT: Beamforming and Power Splitting Optimization for Predictive Control
metadataNote: Crossref current pagination is 4968-4981; older DBLP entry reports 32-45. Current publisher-deposited Crossref record is used.
summary: A multi-antenna base station sends both control commands and energy to aerial vehicles, which divide received power between information decoding and energy harvesting. The design must maintain accurate flight-path tracking while avoiding moving no-fly zones. Stream-function planning first constructs safe reference paths; model predictive control then determines the control inputs. Beamformers and receiver power-splitting ratios are optimized together using successive convex approximation and semidefinite relaxation. The study analyzes the tightness of the relaxation and evaluates the resulting balance between tracking accuracy and harvested energy.

image.title: LAWNs Meet SWIPT: Beamforming and Power Splitting Optimization for Predictive Control
image.caption: Fig. 1: The considered SWIPT-LAWN scenario, where the BS simultaneously delivers control information and wireless energy to a fleet of UASs.

title: Low-Complexity Minimum BER Precoder Design for ISAC Systems: A Delay-Doppler Perspective
originalSiteTitle: Low-Complexity Minimum BER Precoder Design for ISAC Systems: A Delay-Doppler Perspective
summary: How should an OTFS transmitter shape its signal when both reliable data delivery and accurate sensing matter? This paper designs a precoder directly in the delay-Doppler domain, taking advantage of the sparse, slowly varying equivalent channel. The objective minimizes a bound on average bit error rate while meeting transmit-power and sensing constraints. Singular value decomposition separates the design into smaller problems, and a dual optimization method provides a low-complexity solution. The analysis includes feasibility conditions and illustrates the trade-offs among sensing quality, communication reliability, and transmission efficiency.

image.title: Low-Complexity Minimum BER Precoder Design for ISAC Systems: A Delay-Doppler Perspective
image.caption: Fig. 1: The considered OTFS-based ISAC scenario.

title: When UAVs Meet ISAC: Real-Time Trajectory Design for Secure Communications
originalSiteTitle: When UAVs Meet ISAC: Real-Time Trajectory Design for Secure Communications
summary: This paper uses sensing feedback to guide a UAV that communicates securely with a moving ground user. Echo-delay observations feed an extended Kalman filter, allowing the UAV to estimate and predict the legitimate user’s changing location. The flight trajectory is updated to improve the instantaneous secrecy rate in the presence of an eavesdropper following a known path. An iterative optimizer addresses the resulting non-convex design. Numerical experiments assess tracking accuracy and the balance between useful transmission and information leakage.

image.title: When UAVs Meet ISAC: Real-Time Trajectory Design for Secure Communications
image.caption: Fig. 1: A UAV-enabled ISAC system.

title: SDR-Empowered Environment Sensing Design and Experimental Validation Using OTFS-ISAC Signals
originalSiteTitle: SDR-Empowered Environment Sensing Design and Experimental Validation Using OTFS-ISAC Signals
summary: This work takes OTFS-based environment sensing from signal processing to a physical radio experiment. It combines delay-Doppler channel estimation, target localization, and transmitter-velocity estimation in one framework. Fractional delay and Doppler shifts are included in the channel model, and a three-ellipse localization method turns the estimated channel parameters into spatial information. A software-defined radio testbed built with USRP hardware is used alongside simulations to evaluate the design. The experiments compare localization and velocity-estimation accuracy with benchmark approaches.

title: Toward Multi-Functional LAWNs With ISAC: Opportunities, Challenges, and the Road Ahead
originalSiteTitle: Toward Multi-Functional LAWNs with ISAC: Opportunities, Challenges, and the Road Ahead
summary: This article examines how ISAC can support low-altitude networks at both the individual-node and cooperative-network levels. It discusses the gains and trade-offs associated with hierarchical integration, then broadens the architecture to include remote control, edge computation, wireless energy delivery, and language-model-based intelligence. A case study illustrates the benefits of combining these functions. The resulting framework identifies opportunities and open design questions for aerial networks that must support more than data transmission alone.

image.title: Toward Multi-Functional LAWNs with ISAC: Opportunities, Challenges, and the Road Ahead
image.caption: Fig. 1: ISAC-enabled LAWN applications, e.g., accident detection, fire detection, logistics, pedestrian awareness, and live streaming in urban environments, providing flexible and efficient service coverage.

title: On the Interplay Between Sensing and Communications for UAV Trajectory Design
originalSiteTitle: On the Interplay Between Sensing and Communications for UAV Trajectory Design
summary: A group of UAVs simultaneously communicates with and senses moving ground users. This work jointly designs flight trajectories and user association, balancing downlink throughput against tracking accuracy. Range information extracted from sensing echoes supports extended-Kalman-filter prediction and tracking. An alternating optimization method, using successive convex approximation, coordinates the trajectory and association decisions under flight, power, and collision-avoidance constraints. The study makes the sensing–communication trade-off explicit through communication-rate and Cramér–Rao-bound objectives.

image.title: On the Interplay Between Sensing and Communications for UAV Trajectory Design
image.caption: Conceptual illustration of multi-UAV ISAC with EKF user tracking and joint trajectory and user association design, balancing communication rate and tracking CRB.

title: Aerial-networked ISAC-empowered collaborative energy-efficient covert communications
originalSiteTitle: Aerial Networked-ISAC Empowered Collaborative Energy-Efficient Covert Communications
summary: This study combines cooperative aerial sensing with covert communication. Networked UAVs take either information-transmission or jamming roles, while delay and Doppler measurements help an unscented Kalman filter track a moving warden. The design jointly selects jammers, schedules users, allocates transmit power, and plans UAV trajectories. Its objective is energy-efficient downlink communication subject to covertness and power requirements. The framework shows how sensing information and cooperation between UAVs can inform decisions about when, where, and how to transmit.

image.title: Aerial-networked ISAC-empowered collaborative energy-efficient covert communications
image.caption: Conceptual illustration of information and jamming UAVs, ground users, and a mobile warden; UKF tracking supports joint optimization of roles, scheduling, power, and trajectories.

title: Low-altitude wireless networks: A comprehensive survey
originalSiteTitle: Low-Altitude Wireless Networks: A Comprehensive Survey
metadataNote: Author name order normalized against arXiv because Crossref provides many Chinese names in family-name-first order.
summary: This survey treats the low-altitude wireless network as a shared infrastructure for communication, sensing, computation, control, and energy delivery. It reviews network fundamentals and the development of these functions, then examines the metrics needed to evaluate their performance. Privacy and security are considered alongside the practical challenges of organizing three-dimensional airspace and managing aerial traffic. By connecting wireless-system design with airspace operations, the article maps the technical issues that arise when moving from isolated drone links to large-scale low-altitude services.

image.title: Low-Altitude Wireless Networks: A Comprehensive Survey
image.caption: Figure 1: LAWN-enabled scenarios across rural, urban, and offshore environments with satellites and low-altitude platforms collaboratively providing ubiquitous communication, sensing, and service coverage to diverse applications.

title: Formation Control for CRLB-Optimal Cooperative Sensing in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks
originalSiteTitle: Formation Control for CRLB-Optimal Cooperative Sensing in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks
metadataNote: Original site says under review; ORCID and Crossref now provide IEEE TVT DOI and 2026 online publication. Volume and issue are not yet supplied.
summary: This paper asks which UAV formation geometry gives the most accurate cooperative target localization. Starting from range measurements, it derives a Fisher-information model and minimizes the trace of the position-estimation bound. The analysis relates the optimal arrangement to isotropic horizontal information and a regular polygon, with elevation governed by propagation loss and geometric diversity. A distributed controller then brings UAVs toward this configuration while accommodating formation movement and obstacles. Simulations compare localization bounds and convergence against alternative formations.

image.title: Formation Control for CRLB-Optimal Cooperative Sensing in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks
image.caption: Fig. 1: The considered LAWN system where a formation is dispatched to sense the target cooperatively.
